files_changed.summary: Checksums for the new Swagger UI dependency tree.
Replaced the /healthz-only stub with the real surface: GET /healthz and GET /v1/me (200/401 schemas), plus a bearerAuth securityScheme.
Serve api/openapi.yaml at GET /openapi.yaml and mount gin-swagger's UI at GET /swagger/*any pointed at it.
Integration test: Supabase sign-up/sign-in for admin@gmail.com/password, then GET /v1/me through the real router+pool; skips cleanly when Supabase/Postgres/SUPABASE_ANON_KEY are unavailable.

decisions: Used gin-swagger + swaggo/files (UI only) instead of the full swag annotation/codegen toolchain, so the hand-maintained openapi.yaml stays the single source of truth instead of being regenerated from Go comments.

The Swagger UI route is /swagger/*any and the raw spec is served at the top-level /openapi.yaml, not /swagger/openapi.yaml — gin's radix router rejects a static file as a sibling of a catch-all under the same path prefix (confirmed by a runtime panic during manual testing, fixed by moving the spec route out of /swagger/).

api/api.json (Postman collection) was checked against router.go/me.go/health.go and left unchanged — its Health Check, Me - Missing Token, and Me - Authenticated requests already match the current route surface exactly. Per the user's explicit answer in this session, its Postman format was kept as-is rather than redefined as OpenAPI.

admin@gmail.com/password is not seeded anywhere in this repo, so the new test performs an idempotent Supabase sign-up (ignoring an 'already registered' response) before signing in, rather than assuming a pre-existing fixture user.
commands_run: manual smoke test: ran the built binary and curled /swagger/index.html, /openapi.yaml, /healthz, /v1/me
